name: New Year's Problem
description: Vlad has $$$n$$$ friends, for each of whom he wants to buy one gift for the New Year. There are $$$m$$$ shops in the city, in each of which he can buy a gift for any of his friends. If the $$$j$$$-th friend ($$$1 \le j \le n$$$) receives a gift bought in the shop with the number $$$i$$$ ($$$1 \le i \le m$$$), then the friend receives $$$p_{ij}$$$ units of joy. The rectangular table $$$p_{ij}$$$ is given in the input. Vlad has time to visit at most $$$n-1$$$ shops (where $$$n$$$ is the number of friends ). He chooses which shops he will visit and for which friends he will buy gifts in each of them. Let the $$$j$$$-th friend receive $$$a_j$$$ units of joy from Vlad's gift. Let's find the value $$$\alpha=\min\{a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n\}$$$. Vlad's goal is to buy gifts so that the value of $$$\alpha$$$ is as large as possible. In other words, Vlad wants to maximize the minimum of the joys of his friends. For example, let $$$m = 2$$$, $$$n = 2$$$. Let the joy from the gifts that we can buy in the first shop: $$$p_{11} = 1$$$, $$$p_{12}=2$$$, in the second shop: $$$p_{21} = 3$$$, $$$p_{22}=4$$$. Then it is enough for Vlad to go only to the second shop and buy a gift for the first friend, bringing joy $$$3$$$, and for the second — bringing joy $$$4$$$. In this case, the value $$$\alpha$$$ will be equal to $$$\min\{3, 4\} = 3$$$ Help Vlad choose gifts for his friends so that the value of $$$\alpha$$$ is as high as possible. Please note that each friend must receive one gift. Vlad can visit at most $$$n-1$$$ shops (where $$$n$$$ is the number of friends ). In the shop, he can buy any number of gifts.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains an integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases in the input. An empty line is written before each test case. Then there is a line containing integers $$$m$$$ and $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n$$$, $$$2 \le n \cdot m \le 10^5$$$) separated by a space — the number of shops and the number of friends, where $$$n \cdot m$$$ is the product of $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each containing $$$n$$$ numbers. The number in the $$$i$$$-th row of the $$$j$$$-th column $$$p_{ij}$$$ ($$$1 \le p_{ij} \le 10^9$$$) is the joy of the product intended for friend number $$$j$$$ in shop number $$$i$$$. It is guaranteed that the sum of the values $$$n \cdot m$$$ over all test cases in the test does not exceed $$$10^5$$$.
output_specification: Print $$$t$$$ lines, each line must contain the answer to the corresponding test case — the maximum possible value of $$$\alpha$$$, where $$$\alpha$$$ is the minimum of the joys from a gift for all of Vlad's friends.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1619D — New Year's Problem [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
